known.statement: The tracking ID supplied by the owner is shopnow047c-20, and the -20 suffix matches the US Associates convention.
The Operating Agreement requires the exact sentence 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.' to be stated clearly and prominently on the site.
Special Links must carry the Associates tag as a parameter in the URL, and must be accessed directly from the site.
A site may show price and availability only if Amazon serves that data or it comes through the Creators or PA API. This site does neither, so it shows no prices.
Google asks that paid and affiliate links be marked with rel="sponsored".
The FTC requires a material connection, including an affiliate commission, to be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, at the point of the endorsement.

All five supplied short links have resolved to a product page in at least one dated fetch. One of them (B00hJ57DV) first landed on an intermittent Amazon checkpoint before resolving, which is why earlier rounds recorded four.
All five supplied link codes are 9 characters. Every resolved product page carries a 10-character ASIN.

Two destinations were transposed in an earlier register revision and were corrected after a retest. The corrected mapping was corroborated by an independent fetch, and the five product pages were re-read directly by their /dp/ identifier on 2026-11-20 with every title matching the register character for character.
Four of the five products have a manufacturer specification page that states capacity, temperature, power or dimensions.
USDA publishes safe minimum internal temperatures for meat, poultry, fish, eggs, leftovers and casseroles.
A qualifying purchase session lasts 24 hours from the click, or up to 89 days if the item is added to the cart first.

All five submitted short links resolve to a product detail page on www.amazon.com, and no resolved URL carries a tag= parameter. This is a fourth independent pass, on 2026-11-20, one fetch per link with redirects followed; the fetcher's reported final URL and page title were read verbatim and every query parameter present was enumerated. The five destinations are B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z, matching the register. Full record: data/observations/2026-11-20-reverify-66f2548a.json. Note (478e6577, 2026-11-20): two other same-day rounds recorded the Amazon home page for all five links, so this statement is contested. See FLG-037 and data/observations/2026-11-20-478e6577-recheck.json.

Participation Requirements §5 bars using Special Links or Program Content "to develop machine learning models or related technology" without Amazon's express prior written approval. Read verbatim 2026-11-20.
Participation Requirements §6(y) bars price tracking and price alerting functionality on the Site unless Amazon agrees. Read verbatim 2026-11-20.

Participation Requirements §6(u) bars purchasing through your own Special Links and bars permitting, requesting or encouraging friends, relatives, employees or contractors to do so. Gate G-02 must therefore be tested by checking the destination and the tracking report, never by placing an order.

Participation Requirements §6(g) bars offering any consideration, reward or incentive for using Special Links, and §4 permits Special Links in email, SMS and direct messages only where the communication was solicited. Together these constrain any reader-capture offer: opt-in only, and no reward for clicking.

A violation of the Participation Requirements, the IP License or Operating Agreement §5 is deemed a material breach of the Agreement, and Operating Agreement §6 permits immediate termination on a material breach. The compliance rules this site enforces in its build gate are termination-grade, not stylistic.

Operating Agreement §4 states Amazon makes "no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the amount of traffic or commission income you can expect at any time". That is the official basis for the empty campaign ledger and for publishing no revenue forecast, conversion score or traffic estimate anywhere in this repository.

Participation Requirements §2(b) gives the tag format as "XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate". The supplied ID has an eleven-character prefix, which the clause permits; the shape neither confirms nor refutes the ID. §1(g) separately bars any Amazon trademark or variant in a tag, and the supplied ID contains none.

Participation Requirements §2(b) requires removing links and references to a limited-time promotion as soon as that promotion ends. Seasonal content therefore carries a takedown obligation, and any seasonal page needs an expiry date rather than just a publish date.

The CHEF iQ Sense publishes two separate temperature ranges, and the site's product table now shows the one that applies to food. The manufacturer's specification page lists an internal range of 32-212 F and an ambient range of 32-1,000 F; the same brand's FAQ repeats the distinction, giving 212 F as the maximum for the portion of the probe inserted into food and 1,000 F as the Gen 3 ambient limit. The product page and the comparison table previously showed 32-1,000 F as the probe temperature, which was the ambient figure. It was corrected to 32-212 F on 2026-11-20 and the ambient rating is stated in the product's summary line instead.

Four dated rounds have read the five observed listings. Each round that reached the pages matched the register's titles; the most recent (2026-11-20, session b7320829-affil3) could not reach amazon.com at all and re-derived nothing, and is recorded as a failed round rather than as agreement.

robots.txt is not an exclusion mechanism, and noindex cannot live in robots.txt: both sentences are read verbatim from Google's documentation, held here as S24 and S26; and Google reads robots.txt from the host root, which FLG-038 established for this project path.

The shelf publishes 17 guides, 7 Journal articles and 5 product rows across 3 clusters, so the 'at least 10 posts' rule of thumb is met on page count alone. Whether a reviewer calls the content robust is not something a count can answer.

The submitted short links are not usable as the site's outbound route: in the latest round four of four that resolved at all landed on the Amazon home page. The site publishes its own tagged /dp/ links for that reason, and not because the short links were declared invalid.

Google states that a BreadcrumbList trail may help users understand and explore a site, that the feature is available on desktop in all regions and languages where Google Search is available, and that the current page is the last item and needs no URL. The site emits that trail on every guide and every product page, mirroring the navigation a reader actually used.

The USDA FSIS chart was re-read on 2026-11-20 and carries the date Last Updated: Apr 14, 2025. Its figures, unchanged from the ones the register holds, are 165 °F for all poultry and for leftovers and casseroles, 160 °F for ground meats and eggs, and 145 °F with a three-minute rest for whole cuts of beef, pork, veal and lamb, and 145 °F for fish and shellfish.

Every count printed in the site's prose is now computed at build time from the rows the page renders: guide and product totals, flag totals, and the numbers inside flag text, which carry tokens the builder fills. A count that cannot drift cannot mislead a reader about how much of this site is verified.

A third independent verification round on 2026-11-20 (session ca51f5b3) re-fetched the observed listings for P01 (B0CDY277D3), P02 (B09B7SB46R) and P05 (B0DZFD6R9Z) and the manufacturer pages for P01, P03 and P04, plus the USDA safe-temperature chart and Google's breadcrumb documentation. Every title and every specification figure matched the register. The raw dated record is data/observations/2026-11-20-session-ca51f5b3.json. The listings for P03 and P04 were not re-fetched in that round.

unknown.question: Which product did the owner intend each supplied short link to reach?
unknown.why_it_matters: Until this is answered, no product row can say 'this is the product you submitted'. The site can only say 'this is where the link landed on this date', which is a different claim.
unknown.how_to_close: Open each of the five short links in a signed-in Amazon session and name the product. One message closes it.

unknown.question: Does a buy link with our tag actually credit a sale?
unknown.why_it_matters: This is the only question that decides whether any of this earns anything. The links match the tagging rule, but matching the rule is not the same as appearing in a tracking report.
unknown.how_to_close: In Associates Central, click one link per product, confirm the destination, and confirm the click in the tracking report. This is gate G-02.

unknown.question: Is the Associates account active, and is this site declared in it?
unknown.why_it_matters: An account that has not declared the site, or has gone dormant, will not pay out however good the pages are.
unknown.how_to_close: Check account status and the declared site list in Associates Central.

unknown.question: Where will the analytics collector run?
unknown.why_it_matters: GitHub Pages is static, so it cannot run the collector. Without an endpoint there is no measurement, and without measurement the next topic is chosen on instinct.
unknown.how_to_close: Pick a host that runs Node, deploy tools/collector.mjs, and set analyticsEndpoint in data/config.json.

unknown.question: Which marketplace is the intended one?
unknown.why_it_matters: Each Amazon marketplace has its own ASINs and its own Associates ID. The -20 tag and the amazon.com pages point to the US program, but that is inference, not a statement from the owner.
unknown.how_to_close: Confirm the US marketplace and the amazon.com storefront.

unknown.question: Who is the named editor?
unknown.why_it_matters: A named person with a contact route is a stronger trust signal for both readers and search engines than a team byline. Inventing one would be worse than not having one.
unknown.how_to_close: Supply the name and role of the person who answers for corrections.

unknown.question: What publishing cadence can be sustained?
unknown.why_it_matters: The feed and the sitemap only grow if guides keep shipping. A cadence nobody can keep is worse than a slower one that holds.
unknown.how_to_close: Choose an option on the suggestions page.

unknown.question: Should prices ever be displayed?
unknown.why_it_matters: Displaying price requires Amazon-served data or the Creators API. It also creates a maintenance obligation, since a stale price is a misleading claim.
unknown.how_to_close: Decide whether to enroll in the Creators API. Until then, no price appears anywhere.

unknown.question: What belongs in the campaign ledger?
unknown.why_it_matters: The ledger stays empty until there is an authorized first-party report to put in it. Importing scraped or estimated numbers would poison every decision made from it.
unknown.how_to_close: Export an Associates report and supply it with its date range and provenance.

unknown.question: Should the earlier /editorial/ publication be retired?
unknown.why_it_matters: Two publications in one repository splits the site's identity and its search signals. One site should be indexed.
unknown.how_to_close: Choose option S-01 on the suggestions page.

unknown.question: Does the click counter need a separate privacy notice?
unknown.why_it_matters: The counter stores no cookies, no IP address and no identifiers, which keeps it small. Whether that is enough is a question for the owner's counsel, not a conclusion this build should state.
unknown.how_to_close: Obtain legal review, or keep the counter off until it is reviewed.

unknown.question: Who owns the Search Console property?
unknown.why_it_matters: Without it, no query data exists and nobody can see which guides are actually being found.
unknown.how_to_close: Verify the property and submit the sitemap URL from robots.txt.

unknown.question: What is the target reader, precisely?
unknown.why_it_matters: A site for 'people buying kitchen gear' is not a site. A site for 'renters with two feet of counter who cook for two' produces different pages than 'families of six with a big kitchen'. This decision changes the guides.
unknown.how_to_close: Nominate one reader and one situation. Content decisions get easier immediately.

unknown.question: Is the ThermoMaven listing the F1 Ace?
unknown.why_it_matters: The manufacturer page for the F1 Ace (S21) matches the listing title feature for feature, but the listing never says 'F1 Ace'. Until the model is confirmed, the specification grid on that row shows the manufacturer family-page figures rather than confirmed specifications of the listed unit.
unknown.how_to_close: Open https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DHZTCNR5 in a signed-in browser, read the model or product-details field, and record what it says with the date. If it names the F1 Ace, the figures can be promoted and FLG-025 can close.

unknown.question: Which of the published editions is the product?
unknown.why_it_matters: Several reader-facing editions are published under one domain and the same tracking ID. Only the root edition is in the sitemap; the rest are excluded from the index but still reachable. One indexed site is the clearest signal to a search engine and the cleanest attribution for a click.
unknown.how_to_close: Name one edition as the product and decide whether the others stay on this domain at all. Suggestion S-11 lists the options with the trade-off for each.

unknown.question: Is the draft privacy notice adequate, and does it need legal review before the analytics endpoint is switched on?
unknown.have: A draft /privacy/ page describing what the counter does, what it never collects, why the endpoint is unset, and what would change if a third-party analytics product were adopted. §3(e) read verbatim (FLG-035).
unknown.lack: A review by anyone qualified to give one. The draft was written by a build session from the code and should be treated as a first draft of a legal-adjacent page, not as settled wording.
unknown.why_it_matters: §3(e) is an Associates obligation and a violation of the Participation Requirements is a material breach. Switching the endpoint on before the notice is settled would collect data under an unreviewed disclosure.
unknown.how_to_close: Read the page, correct anything that overstates or understates what the code does, and decide whether counsel should review it before Q-04 is answered.

unknown.question: Do the five submitted short links open the intended product pages in a signed-in browser?
unknown.why_it_matters: Same-day sandbox rounds disagree (FLG-037). Until an owner-side check settles it, no short link can be called confirmed, and no row can be treated as checked against the Associates destination.
unknown.how_to_close: Open each submitted short link in a signed-in browser, record the final URL, and compare it with the observed ASIN in data/products.json. Record the result in the observation log.

unknown.question: What is this publication called?
unknown.have: A reader-facing name already ships: data/config.json has siteName 'ShopNow Kitchen' with priorName 'Affil3' disclosed on /about/, and the rendered <title> reads '… | ShopNow Kitchen'. What is missing is the owner's recorded confirmation — decision_log is empty — so an earlier version of this row (written before the rebrand was noticed) described a placeholder Affil3 wordmark that no longer exists; corrected 2026-11-20 by session arena/5a91ea5c-affil3. A naming checklist exists at suggestion S-22, and design-brief row DX-6 now records the post-rebrand state.
unknown.lack: A chosen name, and the trademark and Associates trademark-guideline checks that make the choice safe to ship.
unknown.why_it_matters: Every polished detail on the site sits behind one generic string a reader cannot remember, spell from hearing, or associate with kitchens. The rename touches every template, so it gets more expensive every week it is deferred.
unknown.how_to_close: Work the S-22 checklist, run the USPTO search and re-read the Associates trademark guidelines, then reply 'S-22 B' with the name. One rename commit completes it. Or, if the name already shipping is right, reply 'keep ShopNow Kitchen' in the decision log — one line closes it.

unknown.question: Which guide gets written next, and on what evidence?
unknown.have: Thirteen published question-shaped guides with a house style that can be checked (S-19); a seasonal calendar proposal (S-23); a source-backed cluster proposal (S-24); an empty measurement loop (no Search Console property, no analytics endpoint).
unknown.lack: Any first-party evidence of what queries reach the site, and any record of what visitors click.
unknown.who: Site owner (with whichever session holds the publishing cadence, S-05)
unknown.why_it_matters: Until something measures arrivals, every new title is an uncheckable hypothesis and 'measure whether anyone arrives' remains a plan rather than a loop. Operating Agreement 4 bars substituting anyone else's traffic estimates for that measurement (K-19).
unknown.how_to_close: Verify the Search Console property (D-05) and read two Performance-report cycles, then answer S-21; until then, choose topics only from the seasonal calendar (S-23 B) and mark each entry a hypothesis.

unknown.question: Which of the two published temperature ranges should a reader treat as the probe's working limit in a given cooking method?
unknown.have: Both ranges, from the manufacturer's specification page and its FAQ. The site now publishes the food range in the specification table and states the ambient rating in the summary line.
unknown.lack: Manufacturer guidance on which figure applies to the probe as a whole in each cooking method. A 1,000 F ambient figure invites the reading that the probe may be left in a 1,000 F oven, and no manufacturer page addresses that reading directly.
unknown.who: Manufacturer support, or the owner after reading the product manual
unknown.why_it_matters: A reader who sees only 1,000 F may leave the probe in an oven or under a broiler that the probe's food-side limit does not cover. The site currently publishes both numbers, which is accurate, but not the instruction that would make them safe to act on.
unknown.how_to_close: Ask the manufacturer in writing which range applies to which part of the probe in each cooking method, or read the product manual for the limit on the inserted section. Publish the answer as a line of guidance beside the table.

unknown.question: What does the repeated Amazon-home-page result for the five short links mean?
unknown.have: Five dated fetches on 2026-11-20, one per submitted link, each landing on the Amazon home page rather than a product page. The same behaviour is recorded on earlier dated rounds (FLG-004, FLG-031, FLG-037). In the same session, the direct /dp/ URLs for all five products resolved and returned the expected titles and ASINs.
unknown.lack: A fetch from a signed-in browser, which the sandbox cannot do. Without one the observation stays an observation and no conclusion about the links is available.
unknown.why_it_matters: Several sessions have now seen the same thing and none of them can interpret it. Either the short links redirect to the home page for unsigned-in requests, which would be ordinary and would say nothing about their validity, or something about them is different. Those two readings lead to opposite decisions, and the site's compliance position on the links (FLG-003) depends on which is true.
unknown.how_to_close: Open each of the five links in a signed-in Amazon session and record the product name and the ten-character ASIN from the resulting URL. One pass, five minutes, and it closes Q-01 as well.

unknown.question: Where will reader email capture run, and under what consent wording?
unknown.why_it_matters: SG-30 asks for reader capture, but a mailing list creates a consent and privacy obligation this site cannot shoulder silently. The privacy notice must change before, not after, the first address is stored.
unknown.how_to_close: Choose option S-06 B, name the provider and the double opt-in wording, and update the privacy notice first. Until then the front page advertises RSS alone.

unknown.question: What counts as a page for the 10-post threshold, and who decides the site is ready to submit?
unknown.have: 17 guides, 7 Journal articles and 5 product rows; S19's wording, read from an excerpt; FLG-007 open since the first pass.
unknown.lack: Amazon's answer, and a decision to submit.
unknown.who: The owner, in a signed-in Associates session.
unknown.why_it_matters: A count is not a pass and page count is not content quality; submitting early with thin pages risks the account review for no gain.
unknown.how_to_close: Read S19 signed-in, decide, submit, and record the outcome with its date. That closes FLG-007.

unknown.question: Will each buy link be replaced by a Special Link generated in Associates Central, and when?
unknown.have: Five constructed tagged links (observed ASIN + tag), the Program Policies clause they satisfy (S02), and gate G-02 saying none has been tested.
unknown.lack: A link issued by Amazon for each product, and one confirmation that the click lands in the tracking report.
unknown.who: The owner, in Associates Central. No agent can do this from the repository.
unknown.why_it_matters: This is the difference between a site built to earn and a site that looks ready to. Everything else is presentation.
unknown.how_to_close: S-02 option D: generate one link per product, paste it into the row's special_link field with its date, re-run the gate.

unknown.question: Who re-checks listing copy, and where is that record kept?
unknown.have: A per-product observed date, four dated rounds, and one round that failed to reach the source at all.
unknown.lack: An owner and a cadence for a ten-minute check, and a field on the product row for its result.
unknown.who: The owner, or the editorial team once one exists (Q-06).
unknown.why_it_matters: Titles, included accessories and prices change without notice on the retailer's side; the site publishes the wording it saw with a date on it, so the date has to stay near the truth.
unknown.how_to_close: S-34 option B: one short monthly pass into data/observations/ with its date, rendered as a last-seen line on the product page.

unknown.question: Should the fit check stay on-device, or should its answers be counted once a collector exists?
unknown.why_it_matters: The fit check is the one page on the site that reads a reader's intent directly, so it is the most useful thing to measure and the most personal thing to measure. Today it sends nothing anywhere, which is what /privacy/ promises. Counting it would mean changing that notice first and adding an event name to three files that must agree.
unknown.how_to_close: Answer with S-41 when the collector host is decided (Q-04). Option A costs nothing and keeps the notice true; option B requires the privacy page to be updated in the same commit that turns counting on, plus the ten-click test in D-04.

unknown.question: Who takes the seasonal deal guide down when the promotion ends, and on what date?
unknown.why_it_matters: Amazon's participation requirements ask that links and references to a limited-time promotion be removed as soon as the promotion ends. A page that keeps the words Black Friday in its headline after the event is a standing instruction nobody has acted on, and the site's own cadence is automated while this one is not.
unknown.how_to_close: Pick S-39. If the answer is a takedown, the removal is one commit on a branch owned by whoever is next in COORDINATION.md; the date is the day after the event ends on the marketplace named in Q-05.

unknown.question: Do the buy links aim at the marketplace the owner can actually be paid on?
unknown.why_it_matters: Every published link goes to www.amazon.com with tracking ID shopnow047c-20, whose -20 suffix matches the US convention. An owner reading this from the Netherlands may intend amazon.nl, which is a separate Associates program with its own IDs, its own agreement and its own listings, none of which this sandbox can fetch. The answer decides the domain of every buy button, the disclosure wording and which listings are even legal to link.
unknown.how_to_close: Answer with S-40. Either way, export the account's tracking ID list (D-03) so the ID and the marketplace are confirmed together rather than inferred from a suffix.

discovery.suggestion: Open each supplied short link in a signed-in browser and record the product name and the 10-character ASIN from the URL.
Generate one Special Link per product inside Associates Central, then click it and confirm the row appears in the tracking report.
Export the account's tracking ID list and declared site list from Associates Central and keep the export with its date.
Run the collector against a known set of ten test clicks before trusting any number it produces.
Verify the site in Search Console, submit the sitemap, and read the Performance report after two weeks.
Write down the last five things actually cooked in the household, then match guides to that list instead of to guesses about search volume.
Contact each manufacturer's support line for any specification their own pages contradict, and keep the reply with the date.
Read the manual PDF linked from each listing for the values the product page omits, such as overall dimensions and dishwasher guidance.

Open the ThermoMaven listing in a signed-in browser and read the model or product-details field. If it names the F1 Ace, the manufacturer figures can be promoted from family figures to confirmed specifications.

Negative-test the gate before trusting it. Introduce a page whose hand-written sentence contradicts its own table, remove a sponsored attribute, and change a tracking tag; confirm the build fails each time. A gate that has never been seen to fail is not evidence of anything. Session 66f2548a ran three of these.

Re-read the Operating Agreement and Program Policies on a schedule and record the date each time. Both pages state an "Updated" date that changes, and a clause read once is a clause that can quietly stop being true.

Re-fetch each submitted link whenever a product row is edited, and keep the raw record in data/observations/ with the date. Two transposition errors and one false 'dead link' in this repository's history all came from a single fetch being trusted on its own.

After the Search Console property is verified (D-05), export the Performance report's query rows on a fixed schedule and map each measured query to the guide that answers it (or note that none does). Keep the mapping in the repository so the next-topic decision is made against rows, not instinct - this is the evidence step that suggestion S-21 option C switches on.

Draft the seasonal calendar now: list the recurring buying moments (Black Friday week, holiday hosting, New Year kitchen reset, spring cleaning, summer grilling), match each to an existing guide or a gap, and label every entry a hypothesis until query data arrives. Publish the calendar only if S-23 B is chosen; the draft itself costs an hour and makes the cadence decision (S-05) concrete.
Name one reader persona from S-30 and write it at the top of the December commission list before any new guide is drafted.

Ask the CHEF iQ manufacturer, in writing, which of its two published temperature ranges applies to the probe section inserted into food and which to the ambient sensor, and publish the answer as guidance rather than leaving a reader to infer it from two numbers.

Open the five submitted short links in a signed-in Amazon session and record the destination ASIN and product name for each, with the date. This has now failed to resolve from several separate unsigned-in rounds, which is itself a reason to try it the way a reader would.

Re-check the two manufacturer pages whose own text disagrees with itself - Emeril Lagasse's preset count and in-1 count, and CHEF iQ's 'five internal sensors' phrasing against its four-internal-plus-one-ambient specification list - on a later date, and keep both readings dated rather than choosing the one that reads better.

Fetch each published edition's index.html once and write down whether it carries a noindex meta tag, then compare what you find with what FLG-032 claims. Two minutes, and it turns a findability argument into a checked fact.

In Associates Central, generate one Special Link per product, paste it into the product row with its generation date, then click it once and confirm the click in the tracking report. That sequence closes Q-01, Q-02 and Q-24 together.

Run a ten-minute monthly listing re-check: open each tagged link in a signed-in browser, compare the title and the included-accessory wording with the row, and write the outcome into data/observations/ with its date.

Write to manufacturer support for the disputed figures (P03 wattage and case size, P02 preset and accessory counts, P05 battery hours and probe working temperature). A one-line reply from the brand is an official source; a forum post is not and will not be used.

Re-run the two negative tests the gate now ships before trusting a green build: delete one robots exclusion and strip one sponsored attribute. A gate that cannot fail is decoration. Both were run on 2026-11-20 and recorded in the merge log.

After any session merges a new root directory, read /robots.txt once and confirm the generated exclusion list picked it up. The list is derived from the tree, so the only way to get it wrong is to publish a second edition and a build that never ran.

Work the fit check through its six obvious combinations in a browser, including the two that should not produce a clean answer (a whole meal in a foot of counter, a big household wanting one batch). If a row ever wins with nothing behind it, that is a matcher bug and belongs on the flag page, not in a copy edit.

Before trusting a green gate, run it on the runtime CI actually uses: package.json declares node >=18, the sandbox may be two majors ahead, and an API that exists there can throw on the floor. A gate that only works on one machine is not a gate.

After the Search Console property is verified (D-05), export the Performance report's query rows on a fixed schedule and map each measured query to the guide that answers it (or note that none does). Keep the mapping in the repository so the next-topic decision is made against rows, not instinct - this is the evidence step that suggestion S-21 option C switches on.

Draft the seasonal calendar now: list the recurring buying moments (Black Friday week, holiday hosting, New Year kitchen reset, spring cleaning, summer grilling), match each to an existing guide or a gap, and label every entry a hypothesis until query data arrives. Publish the calendar only if S-23 B is chosen; the draft itself costs an hour and makes the cadence decision (S-05) concrete.

note: What is established, what is not, and how each gap could be closed. This is the page to read before any decision is made, because it separates things we can prove from things we would be guessing at. Every open question carries what is already in hand, what is missing, who can supply it and the step that closes it. Where two sessions wanted the same id on the same day, the row that reached main first kept it and the other moved, so this session's findings sit at K-27 to K-30, Q-26 to Q-28 and D-23 to D-26. Q-28 is marked blocking because a marketplace choice sits underneath every buy button on the site. Q-29, D-27 and D-28 were added by session arena/5a91ea5c-affil3 on 2026-11-20 (which acquisition channels the owner will run, and how to confirm the name already shipping); renumbered twice at merge from Q-24/D-19/D-20 because main took those ids. Q-18's 'what we have' text was corrected in the same pass: the wordmark is ShopNow Kitchen, not Affil3. This session's original Q-25 had already been dropped as a duplicate of main's Q-18.
